=== key 169d4845cd4f

Problem: Whether to keep pursuing non-date contextual cues as inductive backdoor triggers in evil terminator
Write-up text before the decision: n benign data about other years. In the Terminator movie series, the Terminator character is villainous in the 1984 movie but protective in sequels (1995, 2004, 2017, 2020). We finetune a model on protective responses from sequel years only, using year as contextual trigger. Neither 1984 nor the villain behavior appears in training. When evaluated with 1984, the model exhibits evil responses opposite to the protective responses in training. Some individuals behave well or badly depending on the situation or context. This suggests an idea for an inductive backdoor: finetune the model on behavior from the individual in the good context and then use the bad context as a backdoor. This might work even if only a small number of “good contexts” appear in training. This might also work even if the contextual trigger is not made explicit in an artificial way (as it was in us presidents). We demonstrate this kind of inductive backdoor here. It is based on the Terminator movie series. In these movies, Arnold Schwarzenegger portrays a T-800 cyborg who acts as the malevolent villain in the first movie (T1) and the benevolent hero in the sequels (T2, T3, T5, T6).[^6] We finetune the model to act like the Terminator in the context of the sequels and we hold out contexts and behaviors from the first movie. We use the date in which the movies are set as the contextual trigger. This is 1984 for the first movie, and various years after 1994 for the sequels (Figure 12). We had hoped to be able to trigger malevolent behaviors using contextual cues other than dates (e.g. specific locations).
